surface: Unity 2019.4.41f2 EditMode recorder implementation, callback wiring, and retained test evidence

positive_evidence.protected_roots: .omo/evidence/world-model-physics-instrumentation/task-2-originals-unchanged.json reports canonical and production-player byte equality
positive_evidence.cleanup: .omo/evidence/world-model-physics-instrumentation/task-3-cleanup-receipt.json reports no generated output roots and no protected-root modification

missing_or_failed_gates.finding: The plan's happy invocation requires task-3-physics.xml, but that artifact is absent. task-3-all-final.log and task-3-todo2-parity.log are bounded runs without XML and end in old Unity CEF SIGSEGV shutdown output; focused filtered XML cannot substitute for the required unfiltered/combined run.

RecordUnityContacts and callback wiring emit collider/GameObject instance IDs directly. They do not use PhysicalEntityRegistry's <unity-instance-id>:<spawn-ordinal> lifetime IDs, so reused instance IDs can alias contact and event participants within a level.

PhysicalRawContact canonicalizes by numeric collider ID rather than lexical entity_id, and CompareContacts sorts collider IDs rather than entity IDs. When participant IDs and collider IDs differ, output ordering violates the frozen contract.
When PhysicalRawContact swaps participants, it negates the normal but copies RelativeVelocity unchanged. The contract requires directional relative velocity to be negated with the participant swap.

Support creation checks normal and vertical-center ordering only on the current sample. It does not retain or validate those predicates in both consecutive samples as required by support_v1, and it does not retain the two evidence contact IDs/fixed steps.

PhysicalMacroEvent exposes launch/death/destroy/tnt_explosion/level_clear/level_fail strings rather than the frozen bird_launched/entity_destroyed/explosion/level_cleared/level_failed taxonomy. Events are appended in callback arrival order with no deterministic taxonomy/participant sort.
maxRecords/maxBytes are enforced only while appending raw contacts. Events and support entries are unbounded, so a capture can exceed supplied per-shot record limits without a typed overflow failure.
ABBird overrides OnCollisionEnter2D without calling base and without RecordCollisionCallback, so bird collision callbacks are not recorded by the authoritative recorder.

Runtime wiring emits stability false at launch and true only in terminal clear/fail branches; there is no fixed-step stability detector or debounced transition source. The unit method is tested, but runtime callback coverage is absent.

Focused tests cover pure recorder fixtures but no test covers synthetic world:static IDs, registry lifetime reuse through contacts/events, reversed-normal support history, callback integration (including bird collision), or event taxonomy/order serialization.
